sanskrit: divi tārā udabhi śryan sapta sūryasya raśmayaḥ | dhārāḥ samudriyā apas tās te śalyam acucyavuḥ ||
english: The stars flashed forth in the sky, the seven rays of the sun; the ocean's streaming waters — they have dislodged the thorn from you.

sanskrit: īḍe agniṃ svāvasuṃ namobhir iha prasakto vi cayat kṛtaṃ naḥ | rathair iva pra bhare vājayadbhiḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ marutāṃ stomam ṛdhyām ||
english: I praise Agni, rich in good wealth, with reverences; engaged here, may he scatter away what is done against us. As with prize-winning chariots I bring forward my praise; may the hymn to the Maruts proceed sunwise to its fulfilment.

sanskrit: sapta sravanti śiśave marutvate pitā putrebhyo apy avīvatad v ṛtā | ubhe pipṛta ubhe asya rājata ubhe yatete ubhe asya puṣyataḥ ||
english: Seven streams flow for the young one attended by the Maruts; the father has truly guarded his sons. Both protect him, both rule over him; both strive, both make him flourish.

sanskrit: vedaḥ svastir druhaṇaḥ svastiḥ parśur vediḥ paraśur naḥ svastiḥ | haviṣkṛto yajñiyā yajñakāmās te devāso havir idaṃ juṣadhvam ||
english: The vedi is our well-being; the slayer of the deceiver is well-being; the axe is the vedi, the hatchet is our well-being. O gods who have prepared the oblation, who are worthy of worship, who desire the sacrifice — enjoy this offering.

sanskrit: upa priyaṃ panipnataṃ yuvānam āhutīvṛdham | aganma bibhrato namaḥ ||
english: We have come to the beloved, ever-resplendent young one, who grows great with oblations, bearing our reverence.

sanskrit: imā yās te śataṃ hirāḥ sahasraṃ dhamanīr uta | tāsāṃ te sarvāsāṃ sākam aśmanā bilam apy adhām ||
english: These hundred arteries of yours and also the thousand conduits — for all of them together I have stopped up the opening with a stone.

sanskrit: idaṃ khanāmi bheṣajaṃ māṃpaśyam abhirorudam | yenā nicakra āsur- -īndrāṇī kevalaṃ patim ||
english: I dig up this remedy, the māṃpaśya herb that weeps upward, by which Indrāṇī made her husband wholly devoted to her.

sanskrit: akṣyau nau madhusaṃkāśe anīkaṃ nau samañjanam | antaḥ kṛṇuṣva mā hṛdi mana in nau sahāsati ||
english: Our two eyes are honey-bright, the ointment unites our countenances. Bring it within, into the heart — so that the mind of us two shall dwell together.

sanskrit: tvāṣṭreṇāhaṃ vacas- -erṣyāṃ vy amīmadam | atho yo manyus te pate tam u te śamayāmasi ||
english: With the word of Tvaṣṭṛ I have dissolved the jealousy entirely; and also whatever anger is yours, O husband, that too we now calm for you.

sanskrit: vratena tvaṃ vratapate samakto 'hā viśvā sumanā dīdhyo naḥ | taṃ tvā vayaṃ jātavedaḥ samiddhaṃ prajāvanta upa sadema sarve ||
english: Anointed by the vow, O lord of vows, shine upon us all our days with a gracious mind. May all of us, blessed with offspring, draw near to you, O Jātavedas, as you blaze.

sanskrit: prajāvatīḥ sūyavase riśantīr mā vo vidyut taran mota senā | suge tīrthe suprapāṇe pibantīḥ parivṛjya vadhaṃ gohanaṃ carantu ||
english: Fruitful cows grazing in good pasture — let neither lightning strike you nor an army. Drinking at an easy ford with good water to drink, let them roam, avoiding the slaughter of cows.

sanskrit: padajñā sta ramatayaḥ saṃhitā viśvarūpā upa no devīr devebhir eta | imaṃ goṣṭham idaṃ sado ghṛtenā naḥ sam ukṣata ||
english: Knowing the path, calm, assembled, all-formed — come to us, O divine ones, together with the gods. Sprinkle this cowpen, this abode, with clarified butter for us.

sanskrit: yā graivyā apacito atho yā upapakṣiyāḥ | vijāman yā apacitaḥ svayaṃsrasas tā ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: The swellings that are on the neck, and those that are in the armpits, those swellings that are related, that fall of themselves — those we drive away from here.

sanskrit: sāṃtapanā idaṃ havir marutas taj jujuṣṭana | yuṣmākotī riśādasaḥ ||
english: O Maruts, O burners, enjoy this oblation; you who are devourers of enemies, under your protection.

sanskrit: yo no marto maruto durhaṇāyus tiraś cittāni vasavo jighāṃsāt | tasmin tān pāśān prati muñcatā yūyaṃ tapiṣṭhena tapasā hantanā tam ||
english: The mortal, O Maruts, O Vasus, who with evil intent, crossing our thoughts, seeks to slay us — upon him cast those fetters; smite him with your most burning heat.

sanskrit: saṃvatsarīṇā marutaḥ svarkā urukṣayāḥ sagaṇā mānuṣebhyaḥ | te asmat pāśān pra muñcantu sarvān sāṃtapanā matsarā mādayiṣṇavaḥ ||
english: The Maruts who abide through the year, luminous, dwelling in wide space, traveling in their troop among men — may those burners, those inebriating and gladdening ones, release all fetters from us.

sanskrit: dhṛṣat piba kalaśe somam indra vṛtrahā śūra samare vasūnām | mādhyaṃdine savana ā juṣasva rayiṣṭhāno rayim asmāsu dhehi ||
english: Drink boldly, O Indra, the soma from the vessel, O slayer of Vṛtra, hero in the battle of treasures. Partake at the midday pressing, O seat of wealth, and place wealth among us.

sanskrit: yunajmi tvā brahmaṇā daivyen- -āsmai kṣatrāṇi dhārayantam agne | didiḍḍhy asmabhyaṃ draviṇeha bhadrā premaṃ voco havirdāṃ devatāsu ||
english: I yoke you with the divine sacred word, O Agni, sustaining the sovereign powers for him. Shine here upon us with good wealth; speak this our word among the gods who receive oblations.

sanskrit: vi te muñcāmi raśanāṃ vi yoktraṃ vi niyojanam | ihaiva tvam ajasra edhy agne ||
english: I loose your halter, I loose the yoke-strap, I loose the harness. Stay right here, O Agni, incessant one.

sanskrit: prajāpate na hi tvad anyo viśvā rūpāṇi mahinā jajāna | yatkāmās te juhumas tan no astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām ||
english: O Prajāpati, none other than you has brought forth all forms in his greatness. Whatever wish we have when we offer oblation to you, may that be ours; may we be lords of riches.

sanskrit: yat te devā akṛṇvan bhāgadheyam amāvāsye saṃvasanto mahitvā | semaṃ yajñaṃ pipṛhi viśvavāre rayiṃ no dhehi subhage suvīram ||
english: What share the gods apportioned you, O Amāvāsyā, dwelling together in your greatness — fill this sacrifice, O you who hold all that is desirable; bestow on us wealth rich in heroes, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: ghṛtaṃ te agne divye sadhasthe ghṛtena tvā manur adyā sam īdhe | ghṛtaṃ te devā āpyā vahanti ghṛtaṃ tubhyaṃ duhrate gāvo agre ||
english: Ghee is for you, O Agni, in the divine assembly-place; with ghee Manu kindles you today. The water-born gods bring ghee for you; the cows milk out ghee for you at the front.

sanskrit: mayy agre agniṃ gṛhṇāmi saha kṣatreṇa varcasā balena | mayi prajāṃ mayy āyur dadhāmi svāhā mayy agniḥ ||
english: First I take up Agni within myself, together with sovereignty, radiance, and strength. I place offspring within me, lifespan within me — svāhā — Agni is within me.

sanskrit: apsu te rājan varuṇa gṛho mito hiraṇyayaḥ | tato dhṛtavrato rājā sarvā dhāmāni no muceḥ ||
english: In the waters, O king Varuṇa, is your well-measured golden house. From there, O king who holds fast to your vow, release us from all our bonds.

sanskrit: dhāmnodhāmno rājann ito varuṇa no muceḥ ||
english: From station to station, O king Varuṇa, release us from here.

sanskrit: yad āpo aghnyā iti varuṇeti yad ūcima | tato varuṇa no muceḥ ||
english: Whatever we said — 'O inviolable waters,' 'O Varuṇa' — from that, O Varuṇa, release us.

sanskrit: yo rudro agnau yo apsv antar ya oṣadhīr vīrudha āviveśa | ya imā viśvā bhuvanāni cākl̥pe tasmai rudrāya namo astv adya ||
english: The Rudra who is in fire, who is within the waters, who has entered into herbs and plants, who has arranged all these worlds — to that Rudra let there be homage today.

sanskrit: apehy arir asy arir vā asi | viṣe viṣam apṛkthā ahim evābhy apehi taṃ jahi ||
english: Go away — you are the enemy, or you are like an enemy. You have mixed poison with poison; go back against the serpent himself and slay him.

sanskrit: pṛtanājitaṃ sahamānam agnim ugraṃ huvema paramāt sadhasthāt | sa naḥ parṣad ati durgāṇi viśvahā kṣāsad devo 'ti duritāny agniḥ ||
english: We call upon Agni, the conqueror of armies, the overwhelming, the fierce, from the highest seat of assembly. May he, the god, carry us always across all difficulties; may Agni burn away all misfortunes.

sanskrit: yady antarikṣe yadi vāta āsa yadi vṛkṣeṣu yadi volapeṣu yad aśravan paśava udyamānaṃ tad brāhmaṇaṃ punar asmān upaitu ||
english: Whether it was in the atmosphere, or whether it was in the wind, whether in the trees, whether in the shrubs — whatever of the brahman power the animals heard being raised up, may that come back to us.
